# Working on this repository

## Project and source map

This is the bilingual rgive engineering blog, generated by **Pelican** from
Markdown and deployed to GitHub Pages at `https://engineering.rgive.com`.
It is not a Django or Vue application; those technologies appear in articles.

- `content/`: blog articles, named `NNNN_en_topic.md` or `NNNN_fr_topic.md`.
- `content/images/`: logo, favicon, and article images.
- `content/downloads/`: article attachments.
- `pelicanconf.py`: development settings, including the theme, navigation,
  plugins, and language overrides; local URL is `http://localhost:8000`.
- `publishconf.py`: imports development settings, then sets the production URL,
  enables Atom feeds, and deletes the output directory before generating.
- `plugins/i18n_subsites/`: checked-in internationalization plugin, its
  documentation, and `unittest` tests with fixtures.
- `themes/Flex/templates/`: Jinja2 templates; shared fragments are in `partial/`.
- `themes/Flex/static/`: CSS/LESS, JavaScript, fonts, and other theme assets.
- `Makefile`: simplest build and preview interface. `tasks.py` provides
  optional Invoke equivalents.
- `.github/workflows/pelican.yml`: deployment on pushes to `main` or manual
  dispatch, using Pelican's reusable GitHub Pages workflow, `publishconf.py`,
  and `pelican[markdown]`. It does not define a PR test or lint job.

The Flex theme is vendored, not a submodule. Its README, docs, npm scripts, and
tox configuration describe the upstream theme, not the root blog workflow.
Avoid unrelated changes to this vendor tree.

## Setup and verified commands

Run commands from the repository root: configurations and plugin/theme paths
are relative to it. There is no root dependency manifest, lockfile, or pinned
Python/Pelican version. Use a temporary virtual environment rather than
installing into system Python or creating unignored dependencies in the repo:

```sh
python -m venv /tmp/blog-venv
. /tmp/blog-venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install 'pelican[markdown]'
make html
make publish
```

Both builds were verified with Python 3.12.3, Pelican 4.12.0, and Markdown 3.11.
These are verification versions, not project version requirements.

- `make html`: development build into ignored `output/`.
- `make publish`: production build only; it does **not** deploy.
- `make clean`: remove generated output, useful before a fresh development build.
- `make devserver PORT=8000`: rebuild on changes and serve locally.
- `make serve PORT=8000`: serve the site using the development configuration.
- `make DEBUG=1 html`: verbose diagnostics when generation fails.
- `make help`: list all existing Makefile commands.

Invoke requires the additional `invoke` package; `invoke livereload` also needs
`livereload`. Neither is necessary for the Makefile workflow. Do not run
`make github`, `invoke gh-pages`, or `invoke publish` merely to validate:
they attempt remote publishing, unlike `make publish` or `invoke preview`.
The Invoke rsync publishing task also lacks SSH configuration in `CONFIG`.

## Content and multilingual behavior

Follow neighboring articles: metadata is a plain `Key: value` header followed
by a blank line, **not** YAML front matter enclosed in `---`. Existing fields
are `Title`, `Date`, `Id`, `Slug`, `Lang`, `Category`, `Tags`, and `Summary`.
Dates use `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM`; the configured timezone is `Europe/Paris`.

- Use a new four-digit identifier for a new article. Translations share the
  same `Id` because `ARTICLE_TRANSLATION_ID = 'id'`; set their own `Lang`,
  title, summary, and slug. Slugs determine public URLs: preserve existing
  slugs unless the task explicitly changes URLs.
- English is the default site at `/`; French is generated under `/fr/`.
  Some articles exist only in French; do not invent translations.
- Existing categories include English `misc`/`development` and French
  `divers`/`développement`/`communauté`. Preserve the article's language and
  accents, and check generated category links rather than assuming their URL.
- Put article images in `content/images/articles/`, following the existing
  `/images/articles/...` references. `STATIC_PATHS` contains only `images`.
- Downloadable PDFs use `{attach}/downloads/...` links. They are copied as
  attachments even though `downloads` is not in `STATIC_PATHS`; inspect the
  generated article link instead of assuming `/downloads/...` at the root.
  The existing French Wagtail PDF is emitted under `output/fr/downloads/`.
- The plugin hides untranslated articles from another language's listing by
  turning them into drafts. Seeing generated English `drafts/` pages for
  French-only articles is existing behavior, not a missing translation error.

For site-wide changes, inspect `pelicanconf.py` and its `I18N_SUBSITES['fr']`
overrides. For plugin changes, consult `plugins/i18n_subsites/README.rst`.
Keep the Jinja i18n extension and local plugin configuration intact.

## Validation and known limitations

For content, settings, or template changes, run `make html` and `make publish`.
Check `output/index.html`, `output/fr/index.html`, affected article pages,
translation/menu/category links, images, attachments, and production
`output/feeds/all.atom.xml`. A successful build alone does not verify URLs.
Development disables feeds; clean first if checking that old production output
has disappeared. Preview visual changes in a browser.

There is no root linter or Markdown-specific test suite. The existing plugin
suite can be invoked from the repository root:

```sh
python -m unittest plugins.i18n_subsites.test_i18n_subsites -v
```

On the verified environment, eight tests passed and
`TestFullRun.test_sites_generation` failed with
`AttributeError: 'Article' object has no attribute 'category'` during fixture
generation. This is a baseline issue, not an onboarding change. The fixture
also references a `test_data/output` comparison directory absent from this
checkout. Do not remove the test or fabricate snapshots to obtain a pass.
Report this limitation; the actual blog's development and production builds
both pass. To run the eight independent unit tests separately:

```sh
python -m unittest \
  plugins.i18n_subsites.test_i18n_subsites.TestTemporaryLocale \
  plugins.i18n_subsites.test_i18n_subsites.TestSettingsManipulation \
  plugins.i18n_subsites.test_i18n_subsites.TestSitesRelpath \
  plugins.i18n_subsites.test_i18n_subsites.TestRegistration -v
```

Other issues encountered and their handling:

- Pelican, Markdown, and Invoke were absent initially. Installing
  `pelican[markdown]` in a `/tmp` virtual environment enabled both Makefile
  builds without needing Invoke.
- Plugin fixtures warn about unavailable locales, Docutils language `cz`,
  deprecated `{filename}` static links, and missing Czech gettext messages.
  The plugin falls back to `NullTranslations` for missing catalogs. These
  messages did not prevent the eight standalone tests from passing; do not
  misreport the full integration suite as passing.
- `TestRegistration.test_return_on_missing_signal` deliberately logs a
  missing-signal error while passing.
- Flex's `npm test` references a missing `tests/pelicanconf.py` and uses shell
  `source`; it is not the blog validation command. Node is unnecessary for
  ordinary article, configuration, or template edits.

If modifying theme asset sources, inspect `themes/Flex/gulpfile.js` and
`package.json` first. The existing `npm run build` compiles LESS and minifies JS
and Pygments CSS; templates consume `.min.css`/`.min.js`, so source-only changes
may not appear. No npm build was verified during onboarding. Its font-copy
task references `node_modules/font-awesome`, which is not declared in the
theme package manifest; do not assume the vendor build is self-contained.

Keep changes focused. Do not commit `output/`, bytecode, virtual environments,
or installed packages. Review `git status` and the diff before finishing, and
report any command failures and validation that could not be completed.
